title: What happens when you type rfc.akl.run?
description: Every step your browser takes, from keystroke to pixels, and the RFCs that make it possible.
questions: what happens when you type a url in your browser
how does a web page load

steps.title: You type rfc.akl.run
steps.subtitle: URL Parsing & Intent
steps.description: The browser parses the URL into its components: scheme (https), host (rfc.akl.run), and path (/). The URI standard defines how every web address is structured.

steps.title: DNS Resolution
steps.subtitle: Translating name to address
steps.description: Your machine asks a recursive resolver to translate "rfc.akl.run" into an IP address. The query travels through a hierarchy of nameservers — root, TLD (.org), and authoritative — until the A/AAAA record is found.

steps.title: IP Routing
steps.subtitle: Packets find their path
steps.description: With the server's IP address resolved, packets are routed across the Internet. Each router examines the destination IP and forwards the packet hop-by-hop using BGP-learned routes, decrementing the TTL at each hop.

steps.title: TCP Handshake
steps.subtitle: Establishing a reliable connection
steps.description: A three-way handshake (SYN → SYN-ACK → ACK) establishes a reliable, ordered byte-stream between your browser and the server. TCP handles flow control, congestion avoidance, and retransmission.

steps.title: TLS Handshake
steps.subtitle: Encrypting the connection
steps.description: Before any HTTP data flows, TLS 1.3 negotiates a shared secret using a single round-trip. The server presents its X.509 certificate, the browser verifies the chain of trust, and symmetric encryption begins.

steps.title: HTTP Request
steps.subtitle: GET /index.html HTTP/2
steps.description: The browser sends an HTTP request over the encrypted channel. HTTP/2 uses binary framing and multiplexing to send headers (compressed with HPACK) and the request in parallel streams over a single connection.

steps.title: HTTP Response
steps.subtitle: 200 OK — Content delivered
steps.description: The server responds with status 200, content-type headers, and the HTML body. The response may be compressed with gzip or Brotli, chunked for streaming, and include cache-control directives for future visits.

steps.title: Rendering
steps.subtitle: Pixels on your screen
steps.description: The browser parses HTML, fetches CSS and JavaScript (each over their own HTTP streams), builds the DOM and CSSOM, and paints the page. You see rfc.akl.run — every step above happened in milliseconds.
